subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust boundary for outbound-staged generated HTML host-read delivery?
rationale: The code appears fail-closed and well-tested, but it intentionally changes which local HTML files can pass host-read delivery after staging, so automation should not own the final security-boundary acceptance.

options.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
options.body: Approve the current sha256/size SQLite provenance lifecycle and land the PR with the existing regression coverage and proof.

options.title: Require Tighter Lifecycle First
options.body: Ask for additional bounds such as TTL-based row pruning or chunked deletes before accepting the new trust metadata table.

options.title: Keep Staged HTML Fail-Closed
options.body: Decline the boundary expansion for now and leave generated HTML delivery to PDF/Markdown workarounds or a different design.

recommendation.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
recommendation.body: Approve the current sha256/size SQLite provenance lifecycle and land the PR with the existing regression coverage and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and has the strongest feature-history tie to the security-boundary decision.
